title: Automated E-Commerce — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Worksheets for choosing a $1,000-plus evergreen niche, opening vetted authorized-dealer supplier accounts, building true landed cost and contribution margin, shortening the cash conversion cycle, and mapping sales tax nexus before any spend is scaled.

worksheets.title: High-Ticket Niche, Brand, and Supplier Account Plan
worksheets.purpose: Select a $1,000-plus evergreen niche, prove demand and competitor depth, screen brands for MAP discipline and big-box conflict, and open enough vetted supplier accounts that no single brand controls the store's revenue.
instructions: Work the fields in order; the niche and demand checks must pass before any supplier outreach begins.
Use real search tools such as WordStream, Semrush, Similarweb, and Shop Hunter, and paste the actual figures rather than guesses.
Treat every brand sold by Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowe's, or Walmart, or lacking strict MAP, as rejected unless written evidence overturns it.
Run income math at both 0.5% and 1% conversion and apply a 15-20% net margin, never the gross margin quoted by the supplier.
Log every supplier contact by name, date, and touch number so the day-8 call and later follow-ups happen on schedule.

fields.name: niche_price_floor
fields.prompt: List three candidate niches and, for each, the typical retail price of the core product. Mark any niche that is seasonal or whose core items fall under $1,000, and state whether you will drop it or keep it with written justification.
fields.example: Saunas and massage chairs both sit inside the $3,000-$6,000 AOV band, while a third candidate sells mostly in winter. The winter niche is dropped under 'Drop anything that is seasonal or under $1,000' [built with ali — Mf4bZiQ2-Fc @ 00:16:02]. Saunas stay, mirroring Brook Hiddink's sauna and massage chair store that reached about $4.7M in 16 months [Theo Clarke Podcast — 8V2vAoy6GNA @ 00:03:41].

fields.name: demand_validation
fields.prompt: For your lead niche, record the search volume and keyword difficulty you pulled from WordStream or Semrush, whether the trend line is evergreen, and the exact bottom-of-funnel search phrases you would bid on first in Google Shopping.
fields.example: Semrush shows strong volume and low difficulty, matching the rule 'You need high search volume plus low keyword difficulty' [Joe Verschoor — uxvzRhKmdXU @ 00:04:18]. The trend line holds flat year-round, so it passes the evergreen check. First bids go to model-plus-size phrases, because 'Samsung TV 36 in' converts before 'living room TV' ever will [Peak Flow Media — YmrOjrklnxM @ 00:10:02].

fields.name: competitor_benchmark
fields.prompt: Search 'buy [brand] [product]' in the Shopping tab and list every dealer you find. Strike out anyone with a physical showroom or 'appointment required', then name the online-only stores left and estimate their traffic using Similarweb and Shop Hunter.
fields.example: Seven dealers appear; three show 'appointment required' and are struck. The four left include names ending in 'Heaven' and 'Supplies', the real benchmarks [built with ali — pbk_t9e4Xpo @ 00:11:56]. Two are untracked in Shop Hunter, a strong signal because many high-ticket shops run on WordPress sites that spy tools cannot read [WatchMeDropship — xJp0s6G8Hew @ 00:04:30].

fields.name: big_box_and_map_check
fields.prompt: For each brand on your shortlist, record whether Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowe's, or Walmart sells it, then compare the identical model and size across five sellers to confirm the brand enforces strict MAP pricing in practice.
fields.example: Brand A appears at Home Depot, so it is cut, since big-box retailers undercut dealers and outbid them on ads [Asonjf — r79NEO4JF2M @ 00:05:34]. Brand B shows the same model and size at one price across five sellers, so MAP holds, with about 90% compliance at best [built with ali — pbk_t9e4Xpo @ 00:21:56].

fields.name: income_math
fields.prompt: Write your realistic monthly income math: target revenue, assumed average order value, conversion rate, and resulting net profit. Run the numbers at both 0.5% and 1% conversion, and apply a net margin you can defend after every operating cost.
fields.example: At a $1,200 AOV like Kenny's store, 9,000 sessions at 2% produced 199 orders and about $207,953 on $4,376.72 of ads [Asonjf — 91zki-xXArY @ 00:37:42]. The plan models 0.5% and 1% instead, then applies 15-20% net, since 'it's realistic to aim for 15 to 20% net margins' [Joe Verschoor — 5jY7d_1m1t0 @ 00:06:13].

fields.name: dispute_exposure
fields.prompt: For each brand, estimate the dollars you would lose to one chargeback, a restocking fee, return shipping, and labor-warranty claims on a single order. Subtract that exposure from the brand's margin before deciding whether the listing still earns its place.
fields.example: A massage chair brand with a 20% margin carries return freight and labor-warranty claims the dealer absorbs. After pricing one chargeback and one restocking event per batch of sales, the effective margin shrinks, because 'high ticket disputes can really eat away at your margins and your cash flow' [Ecommerce Paradise | High Ticket Dropshipping — EaAeDMJIPLQ @ 00:02:06].

fields.name: supplier_vetting
fields.prompt: Before applying or paying any supplier, verify it exists: check the address on Google Maps, the About Us page, social accounts, Trustpilot, and BBB. Then record minimum orders, drop-ship fees per order, other online retailers carried, and dealer margin.
fields.example: One 'distributor' used a gym photo and an unfinished building as its address, so it was rejected [Marvin — fHLUiiiopmw @ 00:12:24]. A second supplier passed the checks but required a $5,000 minimum and a $20 drop-ship fee per order, which fails the $5,000-plus and over-$15 limits [Ecommerce Paradise | High Ticket Dropshipping — hHXf1_WdANY @ 00:09:24].

fields.name: outreach_cadence
fields.prompt: Plan your batch outreach to 10-20 brands at once. Name the contact for each, ideally the owner or sales director rather than info@, and lay out the follow-up sequence by day, including where the phone call lands.
fields.example: Fifteen brands get applications in one week, expecting 30-50% acceptance [Ecommerce Paradise | High Ticket Dropshipping — hHXf1_WdANY @ 00:17:39]. The GMass cadence runs email day 1, email day 4, phone call day 8, LinkedIn day 12, final email day 18, because the day-8 call converts at 3x a second email [Ecommerce Paradise | High Ticket Dropshipping — hHXf1_WdANY @ 00:12:28].

fields.name: profit_floor_and_price_list
fields.prompt: Once a brand approves you, request its Excel sheet with MAP, dealer cost, and market price. Calculate profit per order for the top three to five sellers, and flag any SKU earning less than your minimum profit per sale.
fields.example: The supplier's sheet lists MAP, dealer cost and market price [Marcus Lam | High Ticket Dropshipping (AI) — ic0HLQbBhQA @ 00:11:13]. Against a $100-200 cost to get each sale, any SKU earning under $500 profit per order is flagged [Marcus Lam | High Ticket Dropshipping (AI) — g_OL9gG7q_I @ 00:01:43].

fields.name: supplier_concentration
fields.prompt: List every approved brand and its expected share of store revenue. Identify whether any single supplier would exceed roughly half of sales, and name the next two brands you will add under your broad store name to dilute that dependence.
fields.example: One sauna brand projects 55% of revenue, the same trap Brook Hiddink hit when a top supplier at about half of sales closed its dealer program in June 2023 [Theo Clarke Podcast — 8V2vAoy6GNA @ 00:27:19]. Two massage chair brands are added under the broad store name, pulling the lead brand below half.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete when at least one evergreen niche above $1,000 passes the demand and competitor checks, three or more vetted brands with strict MAP and at least $500 profit per sale are approved, and no single supplier exceeds half of projected revenue.

worksheets.title: Landed Cost and Contribution Margin Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Replace the supplier invoice with a true landed cost per unit, then carry that figure into a full contribution margin, a target CAC, a break-even point, and a promotion model that cannot quietly lose money.
instructions: Start from units actually received, not units ordered, and spread freight, duty, insurance, and fees across that count.
Insist that invoices list goods value separately from freight and insurance, and record whether the destination values imports on FOB or CIF terms.
Book estimated duty at receipt and correct it against the broker's bill; never leave margin reports running on factory cost.
Keep ad spend alone for ROAS, but load full marketing costs, processing fees, and hidden per-order charges into contribution margin.
Model each promotion as percent-off and as two-for-one, and pause any SKU whose first-order contribution margin to CAC ratio sits below one.

fields.name: landed_cost_per_unit
fields.prompt: Build the landed cost for one purchase order: goods value, freight, insurance, duty, taxes, broker and port fees, and final delivery. Divide the total by units actually received, and record the gap between landed cost and the supplier's quoted unit price.
fields.example: $10,000 of product plus $1,200 freight, $500 duty and $300 fees totals $12,000 across 1,000 units, so 'the true cost becomes $12 per unit instead of the $10 supplier price' [Intel by CandiMentor — CvHvBnjwlJg @ 00:05:57]. That $2 gap, a 20% jump, goes into every margin calculation instead of the invoice figure.

fields.name: duty_stack
fields.prompt: For each imported SKU, list every duty layer that applies: the normal rate plus any Section 301 or other added tariffs. Note whether the duty is charged on goods value only, and flag any SKU containing steel, aluminum or copper.
fields.example: Chinese plastic bins stack a 3.4% normal rate, 7.5% original Section 301 and 12.5% newer Section 301 into 23.4%, or $2,340 on $10,000 of goods [Trade Counsel — -WXoF_u08g0 @ 00:01:56]. A shelving SKU with steel brackets is flagged and its duty rechecked on full customs value, not just metal share [CFOmarketIQ — nUu4s78pX8E @ 00:03:32].

fields.name: invoice_and_valuation
fields.prompt: Record how your supplier invoice and bill of lading separate goods price from freight and insurance, whether your destination values imports on FOB or CIF terms, and whether any quote you received is DDP or export pricing.
fields.example: The factory first sent one bundled figure, which risks freight landing in dutiable value for a US import, so the invoice was reissued with goods listed separately [New York SBDC — LBisYGOUrx0 @ 00:50:28]. For a CIF-valuation destination, import VAT runs on CIF value plus duty, not the invoice price alone [Witners Shipping — 8I51jDAoe-E @ 00:02:06].

fields.name: duty_capitalization
fields.prompt: Explain how estimated duty enters your stock cost at receipt and how you correct it when the customs broker's bill arrives. Record the open entries your broker lists and any protest deadlines on entries already final.
fields.example: Jewelry pieces enter stock with estimated duty at receipt, then get corrected when the broker's bill lands weeks later; otherwise 'every margin report looks better than the truth' [SKUio — DFZ8XDRkuCE @ 00:00:20]. The broker confirms which entries remain open after the Supreme Court ruling; final entries carry roughly six months to protest [CFOmarketIQ — nUu4s78pX8E @ 00:02:43].

fields.name: contribution_margin_build
fields.prompt: Calculate contribution margin per order: net revenue minus product, fulfillment, payment processing, and full marketing costs. Give marketing its own line, including agency fees, influencer and affiliate payouts, and email and SMS tools, separate from the ad spend used for ROAS.
fields.example: ROAS uses ad spend alone, while contribution margin carries influencer payouts, agency fees and email and SMS tools [Bloom Analytics — mWL3C_COYk8 @ 00:01:53]. Processing is audited too: running another merchant on top of Shopify means paying both sets of fees, up to 5 or 6 percent for smaller retailers [Matt Byrne — sR1NjOCbwOA @ 00:11:22].

fields.name: hidden_costs
fields.prompt: List every hidden cost that belongs in your daily contribution calculation, sorted into three buckets: percentage of sales such as royalties or revenue shares, dollars per order such as pick fees, and monthly fixed amounts such as agency retainers.
fields.example: A royalty enters as a percentage of sales, the $2 pick fee as a dollar figure per order, and the agency and influencer fees as monthly costs [Common Thread Collective — b4ddPmPdQcY @ 00:04:08]. Each line is negotiated, since knocking 'a couple dollars out' of one expense 'might be the difference between an extra five dollars per order' [Eric Andrews — 8xfPvprL5qE @ 00:12:53].

fields.name: target_cac
fields.prompt: Derive your target customer acquisition cost from first-order contribution profit minus the net profit you want to keep. Then state your contribution-margin-to-CAC ratio and confirm whether the first order breaks even or better before any lifetime value is counted.
fields.example: First-order contribution of $53 minus a $20 net target leaves a $33 target CAC, a ratio near 1.6. Eric Andrews plans 1.5 at the idea phase and better than 1.0 on the first order [Eric Andrews — gG33a-ErNRQ @ 00:13:30], because then 'all of the subsequent orders... will be pure profit' [Eric Andrews Clips — LKEn47f67vQ @ 00:01:31].

fields.name: break_even
fields.prompt: Divide your fixed costs by your contribution margin ratio to find break-even revenue. Record your gross margin against a 60% target and your break-even ROAS, and note whether contribution margin is above zero at all.
fields.example: $300,000 of fixed costs divided by a 30% contribution margin ratio puts break-even at $1,000,000 in revenue [LedgerGurus: Ecommerce Accounting Experts — e5r7-KT6mQ0 @ 00:02:28]. Gross margin is checked against a 60% KPI, and break-even ROAS against a 1.3 target, with 1.84 called tough to scale [Mark Builds Brands Highlights — eTADhJ3N_oo @ 00:03:21].

fields.name: promo_model
fields.prompt: Model your biggest planned promotion twice, once as a straight percentage discount and once as a two-for-one offer. For each version, record contribution margin per order, subtract CAC, and kill any version whose result goes negative before launch.
fields.example: A brand lost $500,000 running 50% off sitewide one Black Friday [Eric Andrews — t2H3gJHuw6k @ 00:00:00]. Re-run as two-for-one, contribution margin rises from $29 to $69 per order, leaving $36 after CAC [Eric Andrews — t2H3gJHuw6k @ 00:08:56], because 'an extra unit only costs you $21' [Eric Andrews — t2H3gJHuw6k @ 00:07:15].

fields.name: margin_waterfall_decision
fields.prompt: Draw your per-unit waterfall from sale price down to profit after freight, duty, fees, fulfillment and acquisition. Name every step where money disappears, then decide whether this SKU should be scaled, repriced, re-sourced, or paused until unit economics are fixed.
fields.example: A 250 sale ending at 50 means tracing every rectangle until the missing 200 is found [John Galt Finance — 8RBtd8u_F-I @ 00:09:01]. With a first-order ratio below one on a single-purchase product, 'this business should not be scaling until it can fix its unit economics' [Eric Andrews — gG33a-ErNRQ @ 00:15:10], so the SKU pauses for repricing.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete when every active SKU has a reconciled landed cost, a contribution margin above zero after full marketing costs, a first-order contribution-margin-to-CAC ratio of at least 1.0, and a promotion version whose contribution margin minus CAC stays positive.

worksheets.title: Cash Conversion Cycle and Sales Tax Nexus Control Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Measure how many days and dollars stay locked between paying suppliers and collecting from customers, shorten that cycle through better terms, and map every state where economic or physical nexus requires registration, collection, and filing.
instructions: Compute inventory, sales, and payable days from actual period-end dates, and base payable days on purchases rather than cost of goods sold when inventory is growing.
Translate cycle days into working capital dollars and annual interest so every terms negotiation carries a price.
Confirm cash covers the full cycle before any overseas order with zero payable days, and never let an early-payment discount lapse.
Map nexus from both sales thresholds and physical presence, including FBA, 3PL, employees, 1099 workers, reps, and offices.
Keep collection switched off in every state until its permit is issued, and set reminders ahead of each platform's filing cutoff.

fields.name: ccc_calculation
fields.prompt: Calculate your cash conversion cycle as inventory days plus sales days minus payable days. Show each component, the exact period-end dates you used, and whether your payables figure is based on purchases or on cost of goods sold.
fields.example: Day counts come from subtracting period-end dates in Excel with anchored cells, not hard-coded values [Mergers & Inquisitions / Breaking Into Wall Street — rNjMWAOJHwM @ 00:05:07]. Payables use purchases, because a cost-of-goods-sold proxy produced 29.65 days, overstating payment days and shortening the cycle when inventory rose [Understanding Accounting — GtIbksKcl3Q @ 01:06:52].

fields.name: cycle_benchmark
fields.prompt: Compare your cycle against what e-commerce brands typically carry and against negative-cycle operators such as Amazon. Write down how many days of inventory you hold today and whether slow supply chains or wholesale terms are stretching your cycle.
fields.example: E-commerce cycles typically run at least 90 days, with some brands carrying 180 to 240 days of inventory [LedgerGurus: Ecommerce Accounting Experts — F-Y1cubdesE @ 00:04:57]. This store holds about 150 inventory days because overseas shipping is slow, far from the near-zero or negative cycles that Dell, Costco, Procter & Gamble, and Amazon run.

fields.name: working_capital_dollars
fields.prompt: Convert your cycle days into dollars: multiply average daily cost of goods sold by cycle days to find working capital tied up, then multiply by your cost of debt to price the annual interest that cycle costs you.
fields.example: A 65-day cycle times average daily cost of goods sold locks up $59 million of working capital, and at 7% that is 'four million dollars a year just to pay the interest' [InstructorTom — Ju1MGgf9RUw @ 00:03:50]. The same math at store scale shows why 'businesses... definitely fail because they don't have enough cash' [LedgerGurus: Ecommerce Accounting Experts — F-Y1cubdesE @ 00:07:52].

fields.name: supplier_terms
fields.prompt: List each supplier's payment trigger and terms. Note whether you pay on order, on shipment, or on arrival, any early-payment discount offered, and whether you would accept a slightly higher unit price in exchange for longer terms.
fields.example: Kurtis Hanni's client moved to a supplier that billed only once goods reached the warehouse and were sellable, handing back 15 days of credit [Kurtis Hanni — 0WBeNhRVKHY @ 00:11:08]. A 2/10 net 30 discount is always taken, because letting it lapse to hold cash 20 extra days costs 37.2% annualized [One Minute Finance — 7yuWFm95LDw @ 00:07:28].

fields.name: cash_before_order
fields.prompt: Before placing your next overseas order, total the cash that must go out before the first dollar returns. Include deposits, freight, duty, and the full days until customers pay, and confirm cash on hand covers the entire cycle.
fields.example: The 230-day client with zero payable days needed $235,000 out before a dollar returned [Kurtis Hanni — 0WBeNhRVKHY @ 00:09:32]. Cutting shipping from 185 to 15 days and billing on arrival brought the cycle to 45 days, required cash to $67,000, and cash positive into month two [Kurtis Hanni — 0WBeNhRVKHY @ 00:11:29].

fields.name: wholesale_terms_and_exit
fields.prompt: If you are considering net 60 wholesale terms or a future sale of the business, model the receivables jump, the extra inventory build, and your 12- to 24-month average working capital, noting any excess capital to withdraw beforehand.
fields.example: A new big-wholesaler deal on net 60 lets days sales outstanding 'grow tremendously', showing revenue without the cash [LedgerGurus: Ecommerce Accounting Experts — F-Y1cubdesE @ 00:06:05]. Ahead of any sale, the 12- to 24-month average working capital is computed and excess pulled out, or the buyer negotiates to keep it [Brent Freeman  - The CBB Group — KSfESWIcDGI @ 00:09:41].

fields.name: nexus_map
fields.prompt: List every state where you exceed $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions, then add every state with an employee, 1099 worker, rep, office, or Amazon or 3PL inventory location. Note states like California, New York and Texas with higher thresholds.
fields.example: Since June 2018, most states use '$100,000 in sales or 200 transactions,' while California, New York and Texas set higher bars [Cherry Bekaert — rUvJ4UwGqiA @ 00:01:00]. The map adds two states holding FBA inventory and one where a 1099 sales rep lives, since each creates physical nexus [Cherry Bekaert — rUvJ4UwGqiA @ 00:00:24].

fields.name: marketplace_vs_direct
fields.prompt: Split your sales by channel, including your own Shopify storefront. Mark which channels collect tax for you as marketplace facilitators and which leave the obligation with you, and confirm no state has collection switched on before its permit is issued.
fields.example: Amazon, Walmart and Etsy sales are marketplace-collected, since 'a major marketplace like Amazon is already taking care of sales tax for you', but Shopify is not a facilitator [Avalara — QiT660QtcXA @ 00:01:18]. Collection stays off in each new state until the permit arrives, because collecting unregistered creates personal officer liability [Avalara — EtT3YoVfP0c @ 00:19:36].

fields.name: tax_engine_choice
fields.prompt: Choose your calculation and filing stack for the next year. Record the monthly subscription, per-filing or per-return cost, whether one tool handles both engine and filing, and which questions you will ask in negotiation, such as SST CSP enrollment.
fields.example: TaxJar starts near $20 a month with AutoFile at about $30 to $35 per filing [Arthur Glinkin — 1Cr_iHc8p4s @ 00:07:44], and runs as both engine and filer since its returns cannot be adjusted [LedgerGurus: Ecommerce Accounting Experts — 1L7s6llWlRo @ 00:14:42]. Avalara's $10k to $30k engine waits until revenue passes $5M.

fields.name: filing_calendar
fields.prompt: Build your monthly filing calendar. Note each platform's return-approval cutoff, which report serves as your source of truth when ledgers disagree, any prepayment discount you can take, and whether your provider offers hands-on audit defense.
fields.example: Returns are approved before TaxJar's 5th-of-month deadline, while Avalara auto-files after the 11th at 5 PM ET [LedgerGurus: Ecommerce Accounting Experts — -DhtTN5_Rh4 @ 00:12:28]. The Detailed Sales Tax Analysis report beats QuickBooks Online when they disagree [Arthur Glinkin — 1Cr_iHc8p4s @ 00:09:04], and Texas prepayments earn a 1.25% discount [Avalara — EtT3YoVfP0c @ 00:49:10].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete when the cycle is calculated in both days and dollars, cash on hand covers the next order's full cycle, every nexus state is registered before collection begins, and a filing calendar naming the tool, cutoff, and source-of-truth report is in place.

worksheets.title: Fulfillment Partner Selection and Back-Office Automation Plan
worksheets.purpose: Decide whether and when to hand fulfillment to a 3PL, price the true invoice rather than the headline pick rate, prove inventory sync before volume flows, and chain the post-order back office together without falling for done-for-you automation schemes or leaving product liability gaps.
instructions: Pull the last 90 days of order data, including items per order, weekly packing hours, and shipping cost per order, before filling in any field.
Request written quotes from at least three 3PLs and itemize every fee line, not just the advertised pick and pack rate.
Run the timed test orders, the five-order sync trace, and the phased transfer before moving full inventory or full order volume.
Document every automation step with its tool, trigger, and duplicate-prevention test, so a re-run never creates duplicate customers, invoices, or stock changes.
Screen every automation seller and insurance policy with the checks listed below, and sign nothing until the completion gate is met.

fields.name: self_fulfillment_ceiling
fields.prompt: Record your current monthly order count and weekly hours spent packing. Compare both numbers against the self-fulfillment ceiling of roughly 100 to 500 orders a month or 15 to 20 weekly packing hours, and state whether you have crossed it.
fields.example: We ship about 320 orders a month and spend roughly 18 hours a week packing in the garage, which puts us inside the ceiling band on both measures. Smart Capital prices pick and pack at $2 to $5 plus about $1 per extra item, so we are now requesting quotes [Smart Capital — 8R8um_CLrWI @ 00:33:10].

fields.name: per_order_cost_model
fields.prompt: Build a side-by-side per-order cost model comparing self-fulfillment against a 3PL quote. Include your own time valued at an hourly rate, packaging, postage, pick and pack fees, and per-item charges, then state the per-order difference in dollars.
fields.example: Using Olivia's spreadsheet logic for 300 one-item orders a month at a $40 average price, self-fulfillment lands near $15.50 per order once about $6 of owner time at $20 an hour is included, against about $12 through a 3PL. That gap of roughly $3.50 per order funds the switch [Smart Capital — 8R8um_CLrWI @ 00:33:10].

fields.name: true_invoice_profile
fields.prompt: List every fee line a candidate 3PL could bill against your real order profile: multi-line orders, bundles, inserts, returns, bin and pallet storage, receiving, account minimums, and manual edits. Note which fees the headline pick rate hides.
fields.example: Our average basket holds three items, bundles ship with a printed insert, and about one order in ten needs a manual edit. Quote B beat everyone on pick and pack by a dollar, but its storage, receiving and returns fees recovered that dollar and more. We priced the whole invoice, not the headline rate [SHIPHYPE Fulfillment — CB8e30IUILU @ 00:00:40].

fields.name: multi_item_fit_check
fields.prompt: Calculate your average items per order and the per-item pick fee each 3PL charges. Decide whether multi-item baskets make outsourced fulfillment cost prohibitive for your store, the way one merino apparel brand concluded, and record the decision.
fields.example: Unbound Merino co-founder Dan rejected 3PLs because the average order carries three or more items, and paying for every item picked made outsourcing too expensive. Our basket averages 1.2 items, so at $2 to $5 plus about $1 per extra item the math still favors the 3PL. Decision: outsource, recheck quarterly [Learn With Shopify — 088tKYu7kKY @ 00:08:16].

fields.name: delivery_speed_test
fields.prompt: Describe the delivery speed test you ran before signing. Record the dates and arrival times of a $10 test order to your own address and one to a friend in another region, and confirm the coverage map and cutoff time are written into the agreement.
fields.example: Two $10 orders went out on a Monday: one to our office, one to a friend three time zones away. The local parcel arrived Wednesday and the distant one Friday, slower than the sales call promised. We asked for the coverage map and the 2 p.m. cutoff in the service agreement, not just an email [Smart Capital — 8R8um_CLrWI @ 00:15:15].

fields.name: phased_inventory_transfer
fields.prompt: Plan your phased inventory transfer to the new 3PL. State what share of stock moves first, how many weeks you will run it, which delivery-time and error-rate figures you will measure, and what result releases the remaining inventory.
fields.example: We will ship about a third of our 1,800 units in the first inbound, roughly 600, and run live orders against it for three weeks. We will track average delivery days by region and the mis-pick rate. If both hold to quoted levels, the remaining 1,200 units move in week four [Smart Capital — 8R8um_CLrWI @ 00:19:08].

fields.name: sku_sync_trace
fields.prompt: Document your SKU sync test between the store and the warehouse system. Place five test orders with different products, quantities and one out-of-region address, trace each from store to doorstep, and list every SKU mismatch you found and fixed.
fields.example: Five test orders surfaced two silent failures. Our store listed 'Navy-M' while the warehouse used 'NVY-MED', and a gift bundle sat as one SKU in Shopify but two SKUs in the warehouse. Neither threw an error; both simply never released to pick. We renamed the size code and split the bundle mapping [Smart Capital — 8R8um_CLrWI @ 00:22:52].

fields.name: order_to_ledger_chain
fields.prompt: Map the automation chain that runs after a paid order. List each step from the Shopify order to customer record, sales order, invoice, task card and team alert, name the tool handling it, and describe your duplicate-prevention acceptance test.
fields.example: A scheduled Claude prompt reads each paid Shopify order, creates the customer and sales order in Zoho Books, raises the invoice, opens a Trello card and pings Slack. Because Zoho Books updates both ledger and stock, we skip a separate inventory link. Acceptance test: re-run an already-processed order and confirm zero duplicate customers or invoices [Fazil Automates — 4OmfNbuCmDQ @ 00:04:06].

fields.name: inventory_forecast_inputs
fields.prompt: For each top SKU, record the forecasting inputs your planning tool needs: supplier, lead time, days of cover, safety stock, and ABC grade. Note how you removed stockout days from the base period before projecting growth from past sales.
fields.example: SKU A-101 is an A-grade item from our main vendor with a 45-day lead time, 60 days of cover and 14 days of safety stock. It sold out for 11 days in March, so we cut those days from the base period before projecting growth, otherwise the forecast would understate true demand [Davie Fogarty — 313GvO3pScc @ 00:47:48].

fields.name: automation_vendor_and_liability_screen
fields.prompt: Screen every automation seller and insurance policy before committing money. Record the result of searching each seller's name plus 'FTC', any upfront fees or income claims, and whether your product liability policy, not just general liability, excludes any states.
fields.example: A done-for-you Walmart pitch asked $50K upfront against a projected $100K a year, plus inventory and a 70/30 split. Searching the company name plus 'FTC' was our walk-away trigger. Separately, the cheapest product liability quote excluded New York and Colorado, two highly litigious states, so we paid more for full coverage [Coffeezilla — fPLMdewUMQw @ 00:02:25].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 4 is complete when the per-order cost comparison, full-invoice fee list, two timed test orders, five traced sync orders, phased transfer plan, duplicate-safe automation chain, and written product liability coverage are all recorded, and no automation seller under consideration has failed the FTC search.

worksheets.title: Returns, Chargebacks, and Retention Systems
worksheets.purpose: Turn returns and chargebacks into a budgeted, documented line item, route support tickets between AI and humans with hard rules, price AI support honestly, and build post-purchase and subscription flows that chase the profitable second order.
instructions: Publish the return policy before the first sale and keep a dated copy of every version that goes live.
Size the returns reserve from your real 90-day data where available, and fund it weekly into a separate account.
Build the chargeback evidence pack as a reusable template so every dispute is filed inside the evidence window.
Write AI routing rules as hard rules, not suggestions, and test them against past tickets before launch.
Build post-purchase flows in Klaviyo with cancel and refund filters in place before turning any flow live.

fields.name: return_policy_terms
fields.prompt: Write the plain-language return policy you will publish before the first sale. State the return window in days, who pays return shipping, which items qualify, and the refund forms you accept, such as store credit, exchange, or original payment.
fields.example: Our policy offers a 30-day window from delivery, buyer-paid return shipping on change-of-mind returns, and free exchanges on wrong sizes. Refunds go to store credit first, then the original payment method on request, because store credit is usually much faster to settle. The policy is live on the footer page before launch day [Tutorial Stack — YnEcCYA-UDs @ 00:02:51].

fields.name: returns_reserve_sizing
fields.prompt: Size your weekly per-order returns reserve. Use 90 days of real return data if you have it, or the planning benchmark for your category, then show the reserve per order in dollars and the weekly amount you will set aside.
fields.example: We sell apparel online, so we plan on 20% returns rather than the 19.3% all-category average. At a $60 average order and an estimated $15 net loss per returned order, the reserve is $3 per order. At 250 orders a week, we move $750 into a separate returns account every Monday [Dropshipping Deep Dive — 1L4TNDjsICQ @ 00:27:46].

fields.name: refund_without_return_rules
fields.prompt: Set your refund-without-return rules by item value. Define the dollar threshold below which you refund and let the customer keep the item, and the partial-refund offer you make on higher-value items the supplier will not take back.
fields.example: Items under $20 get an immediate refund with no return, because reverse shipping costs more than the product and return friction is not justified. Above $20, where the supplier refuses returns, we offer 50% back with no shipping required, since most customers prefer some money now over packaging and a post office trip [Shopify Mastery — EjZsqaOIDsc @ 00:07:07].

fields.name: supplier_damage_window
fields.prompt: Record each supplier's damage-dispute window and photo requirements. Note how many days after customer receipt you have to file, any longer window for electronics, and the internal alert that ensures a damaged-item claim is filed before the window closes.
fields.example: CJ allows 3 days from customer receipt to dispute damage, or 7 days for electronics. Miss it and we carry the entire cost instead of sharing it with the supplier. Our help desk tags any 'damaged' ticket urgent and requests customer photos the same day, so the claim reaches CJ inside 48 hours [Dropshipping Deep Dive — 1L4TNDjsICQ @ 00:13:07].

fields.name: chargeback_evidence_pack
fields.prompt: Assemble your standard chargeback evidence pack. List every document you will attach to a dispute, where each one is pulled from, how long the pack takes to build, and how you confirm tracking was visible to buyer and payment provider.
fields.example: Each dispute pack holds the Shopify order export, supplier tracking, a carrier delivery screenshot, the Stripe or PayPal transaction record, and copies of every customer email, which takes about 10 to 15 minutes. Shopify Payments charges $15 per chargeback and pulls the disputed amount from the next payout, so we file inside the evidence window [Flying Start Online — rhATJAycfEU @ 00:13:15].

fields.name: ai_ticket_routing_rules
fields.prompt: Define which ticket types your AI agent may resolve alone and which must hard-route to a human. Include order-status questions, damaged or wrong items, address changes, refunds above your dollar limit, angry customers, and chargeback threats, with one routing reason for each.
fields.example: The AI answers 'where is my order' tickets by sending the tracking link, never a promised delivery date, because Shopify holds the tracking number rather than the latest carrier scan. Delivered-not-received, damaged or wrong items, address changes, cancellations, anger and chargebacks all route to a human, and refunds over $75 enter a manager approval queue [Macha — VsY0GsB1UI0 @ 00:05:00].

fields.name: ai_pricing_breakeven
fields.prompt: Model the monthly cost of AI support under per-resolution pricing and flat pricing. Use your real ticket volume and an honest resolution-rate estimate, then state the resolution rate at which each pricing model becomes the cheaper option.
fields.example: We receive about 750 tickets a month. Gorgias AI Agent bills $1 per automated interaction on monthly billing, or $0.90 annual, so the AI part of the bill grows with every resolution. Macha starts at $299 for 750 tickets and breaks even against Gorgias only near 50% resolution, so our pilot must prove that rate first [Macha — iqOjQraqwcM @ 00:05:42].

fields.name: post_purchase_flow_design
fields.prompt: Design your Klaviyo post-purchase flow step by step. Give the delay before each email, its purpose, any offer and its expiry, when the review request fires, and the filters that keep cancelled or refunded buyers out of the sequence.
fields.example: Email one is a thank-you after order. Email two carries a cross-sell offer that lasts three days, followed by a 24-hour last chance. The review request waits until the product has been in hand about 7 to 10 days after delivery. Flow filters require canceled zero and refunded zero since starting [Tarun Brar - eCom Email Marketing — coevagBV6wU @ 00:15:48].

fields.name: second_order_window
fields.prompt: Set the target window for each customer's second purchase and the touchpoints that drive it. State the number of days, the profit difference between first and second orders in your store, and the share of revenue email should carry.
fields.example: Loyalty runs much higher when a buyer purchases again within 30 to 60 days, so our replenishment and cross-sell emails all land inside day 45. At a 3x ROAS our first order leaves about $26, while the second order earns about $60. We target email at 35 to 50 percent of attributed revenue [Derek Stroh — cerX0RFHJ0c @ 00:09:35].

fields.name: subscription_retention_plan
fields.prompt: If you sell replenishable products, outline your subscription retention plan. Describe the subscription platform, the flows that fire around renewal and cancellation, and the three-month milestone you will track, since early tenure strongly predicts longer customer life.
fields.example: We pair Recharge with Klaviyo, modeled on the Scooch result where churn fell 33%, subscriber LTV tripled and ad spend dropped 48% while revenue slipped 5%. Our flows remind subscribers before renewal and offer a skip before cancellation. We track the share reaching month three, because customers kept three months tend to stay longer [Milan Raviji│Klaviyo & Email Marketing — 6xiaPZPDBCQ @ 00:06:42].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 5 is complete when the return policy is live, the weekly returns reserve is funded, every supplier damage window is logged, the chargeback evidence template exists, AI routing rules and the pricing break-even are documented, and every post-purchase flow excludes canceled and refunded buyers.

worksheets.title: Shopping Feed Optimization and Scaling Gates
worksheets.purpose: Treat the product feed as the targeting layer for Shopping and Performance Max, protect the account from suspensions and lost product history, then lift conversion and scale spend only when breakeven ROAS, CAC payback, and fulfillment capacity say the math works.
instructions: Export your Merchant Center feed and search terms report before editing any title, price, or identifier.
Make one change per SKU at a time and give each test one to two weeks with enough budget to read the result.
Lock product IDs and confirm sale prices match the live site before every sync or app migration.
Measure conversion rate and page load speed before running any other conversion experiment.
Do not raise ad budgets until breakeven ROAS, CAC payback, and fulfillment surge capacity are written down and pass.

fields.name: title_rewrite_plan
fields.prompt: Rewrite the Shopping titles for your top five products. For each, record the current title, the converting search term pulled from your search terms report, and the new title that front-loads that term while using most of the 150 characters.
fields.example: Home Reserve retitled its 'Alley sofa' listing to a kid and pet friendly washable sectional sofa and saw a 10x jump in clicks and impressions, with sales rising. Our 'Nordic Parka' becomes 'Men's Waterproof Insulated Winter Jacket - Nordic Parka', matching the search term that already converts, with size and color filling the remaining characters [Grow My Ads — hY8ZBC3A4uQ @ 00:10:45].

fields.name: feed_attribute_integrity
fields.prompt: Audit the feed attributes that must match your live site exactly: price, sale price, and availability. Record how often you check them, which tool syncs the catalog, and where edits must be made so the next sync does not overwrite them.
fields.example: We add a sale price to every product because the green sale price boosts clicks, but a mismatch with the website gets the product suspended. DataFeedWatch runs our catalog, so edits happen inside the app, since manual Merchant Center changes get overridden on the next sync. Prices are checked against the live site every Monday [Max Crakanthorp — H4yH9xs030Q @ 00:13:46].

fields.name: product_id_and_identifier_lock
fields.prompt: List the product IDs you have locked before any feed cleanup or app migration, and record the identifier plan for products without a GTIN, including the unique MPN format you will assign so Google keeps learning about each product.
fields.example: Before moving from the native channel to a feed app, we exported every product ID and mapped the app to reuse them, because a changed ID creates a new product for Google and performance drops. Our house-made accessories have no GTIN, so each gets a unique MPN in the format BRAND-CATEGORY-0001 rather than a blank identifier [KeyCommerce — S1NhYxaPnic @ 00:06:21].

fields.name: custom_label_segments
fields.prompt: Define the custom labels you will apply to segment the catalog for bidding. Specify each label's values for margin tier, price bucket, and season, the tool that writes them, and any bucket that deserves its own target ROAS.
fields.example: Custom label 0 holds margin tier: high above 30%, mid at 15 to 30%, low below 15%. Label 1 holds price buckets from 100 to 10,000, with a 2,000-plus bucket carrying its own tROAS. Label 2 marks winter, summer or evergreen. A Google Sheets supplemental feed writes all three [Tim Sutton | Google Ads | Launchpresso — APb0cOGKROE @ 00:05:06].

fields.name: merchant_center_approval_checklist
fields.prompt: Confirm every store page and business detail Merchant Center reviews before approval. Record the live URL for contact, refund, shipping, privacy and terms pages, where business details appear, and any promotion end times set to avoid early cutoffs.
fields.example: Contact, refund, shipping, privacy and terms pages are all linked in the footer, and our business address and phone number show on the contact page, because a perfect feed alone does not guarantee approval. Our Black Friday promotion ends at 11:59 p.m., since Google ends promotions at midnight the day before [Wixpa Google Shopping Feed — RHJvGN_6sf0 @ 00:04:47].

fields.name: title_test_discipline
fields.prompt: Plan a controlled title test. Name the SKU, the single change you will make, the test length in weeks, the daily budget behind it, and the metrics you will read, including CTR, CPC, conversion rate, and ROAS, before calling a winner.
fields.example: We will change only the title on our best-selling jacket SKU and hold everything else steady for two weeks. Because $40 to $50 a day is not enough data, the test runs at $150 a day. We compare CTR, CPC, conversion rate and ROAS against the prior two weeks before deciding [Ecom Chris — d9kULGtUBD4 @ 00:28:56].

fields.name: conversion_baseline_and_speed
fields.prompt: Record your current store conversion rate against the 1 to 3% average and the 6 to 8% top tier. Then log your mobile page load time, the largest speed drag found, and the estimated conversion loss from each second of delay.
fields.example: Our store converts at 1.4%, inside the 1 to 3% band but far from the 6 to 8% top tier. Product pages load in 4.2 seconds, mostly from oversized high-resolution images. At a 7% conversion loss per second of delay, compressing images with Tiny Image Optimizer comes before any other CRO test [Chase Chappell — daDsoHXE52A @ 00:01:49].

fields.name: breakeven_roas_by_budget
fields.prompt: Calculate breakeven ROAS for three planned monthly ad budgets using your fixed costs and variable margin. Show the arithmetic for each level, then state which budget you will fund and the MER you will watch instead of pixel attribution.
fields.example: In Callinan's model, breakeven ROAS runs 22 at $10k of spend, 6 at $50k and 4 at $100k, because fixed costs spread across more contribution as spend rises. Our version uses $40k of fixed costs and a 40% variable margin. We will fund the middle budget and judge it on blended MER, not pixel-reported ROAS [Adam Callinan — VCXWZQgbKXw @ 00:25:39].

fields.name: cac_payback_gate
fields.prompt: Calculate CAC payback in days for your current acquisition channels. State whether it falls inside the 30 to 60 day window, and if it runs six months or longer, name the working capital source that will finance growth.
fields.example: Our blended CAC is $48 and each first order contributes $30 before acquisition cost, so $18 remains unrecovered until the second order, which typically lands around day 50. That places payback at roughly 50 days, inside the 30 to 60 day window, so we can scale without lining up outside working capital first [Leading Social — KpmUvCBEKK4 @ 00:01:48].

fields.name: scaling_readiness_gate
fields.prompt: Before increasing spend, record your scaling readiness: months of flat revenue, MER trend, fulfillment capacity for surge volume including separate picking and packing checks, and whether you will scale in-house or bring in an agency, with your reasoning.
fields.example: Revenue has sat near $80k a month for three months while MER keeps rising, the signal to bring in an agency instead of forcing more self-run spend. Our 3PL has confirmed a separate picker and packer for the holiday surge, giving two points of verification. We will pull back 5% of marketing spend in cyber [Growth Manifesto Podcast — 7v_KO8bj_G0 @ 00:29:01].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 6 is complete when the top five titles are rewritten around converting search terms, price and product ID integrity checks are scheduled, custom labels are live, approval pages are confirmed, a controlled title test is planned, and breakeven ROAS, CAC payback, and surge fulfillment capacity all pass before any budget increase.
